In an emotional speech during his solo induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on Saturday, the former Genesis frontman addressed “rumors” about his ability to tour as health issues have sidelined him from shows since 2022.

“You haven’t heard the last of me, I can promise you that,” Collins told the crowd at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater.

Collins — who was first inducted into the hall of fame with Genesis in 2010 — was reportedly tearful and received a standing ovation as Blink-182 drummer Travis Barker honored him in an introduction.

Barker noted that Collins’ array of hits inspired him as a drummer and praised him for “arguably the most badass drum fill of all time” on “In the Air Tonight” before covering the song as Cynthia Erivo joined him on the mic.

Collins — who revealed this year that he had a near-death experience when he was hospitalized in 2024 due to alcohol abuse-linked complications — later took the stage using canes before joking to the crowd that it’s “really not as bad as it looks” and lifting the canes above the podium.

“I’m much better,” he said.

He thanked his assistant, Lindsay Evans, for saving his life and advising him on how to live “better,” adding that he now considers himself a “well man.”

His children Lily, Nicholas and Joely Collins attended the ceremony.

“I’ve really been just very, very lucky. I grew up just wanting to play the drums,” he said. “That’s all I wanted to do. Everything else has been a very happy accident.”

Collins told reporters that his drumming days are “probably done” but didn’t rule out future concerts altogether.

“Just the other night I was talking to the kids about it, and everyone got excited, including myself. That it’s not beyond the realm of possibility of doing some shows,” he said.

“I’ve got some great friends of mine that are great musicians that have been in my band, and I’d like to get down to my studio just to have some fun and write some music that I hope will be good enough for people to hear and sort of enjoy. So it’s a work in progress.”

The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony is set to air Thursday, Dec. 8 on ABC. Other inductees in the 2026 class include Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Oasis, Sade, Luther Vandross, Wu-Tang Clan and more.
